title: Selecting text in the terminal copies it
description: Make sure you can copy what it prints — everything you paste back into the wizard later depends on it
note: Step two: open another one, select the code, paste it back (button: Open and send a test line)

steps.title: Press "Open and send a test line" on the card
detail: The button on the right of this row
It opens a new window and sends one line for you automatically

visual.caption: The button sits on the right of that step's header row

kids.title: A new terminal window opened
detail: It often doesn't come to the front — this window hides it. Nothing is broken
Look for the terminal icon in the Dock and click it; a dot under the icon means it's running
Still can't find it? Press F3 to spread out every open window

visual.caption: The terminal icon in the Dock, with a dot under it

kids.title: A new terminal window opened
detail: It often doesn't come to the front — it just flashes in the taskbar. Nothing is broken
Click the flashing item in the taskbar and it pops up

kids.title: A line of code is printed
kids.detail: One line of letters and numbers, like this

visual.caption: That line printed in the terminal

steps.title: Select that whole line with the mouse
detail: Drag from the start of the line to the end so the whole line is highlighted
It's copied the moment you release the mouse

visual.caption: The whole line highlighted — catch both ends

kids.title: Ctrl+C here is not copy
detail: In this mode Ctrl+C isn't copy — it interrupts what's running
Pressing it stops Claude Code, and you'd have to start it again
Selecting and releasing the mouse has already copied it

steps.title: Go back to the wizard and paste it into the field on the card
steps.detail: The input box just below this row

kids.title: If it matches, this row ticks itself
detail: If it doesn't match, it tells you straight away
You didn't do it wrong — usually the selection missed one end. Select the whole line again

steps.title: Close the two terminal windows you just opened
steps.detail: Every verification opens a new one. Close them as you go and they're easier to find later
